questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual elemento do mapa explica o significado dos símbolos e das cores?
questions.hint: É como um 'dicionário' do mapa.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Para que serve a escala de um mapa?
options: Mostrar quantas vezes a área real foi reduzida
questions.answer: Mostrar quantas vezes a área real foi reduzida
questions.hint: Pense em distância no papel e distância real.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual elemento indica o assunto e o lugar representado no mapa?
questions.hint: Geralmente fica no alto do mapa.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na rosa dos ventos, qual ponto cardeal fica oposto ao norte?
questions.hint: Pense no ponto que fica 'embaixo' na maioria dos mapas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um ponto colateral?
questions.hint: Os pontos colaterais ficam entre dois pontos cardeais.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que direção o Sol nasce, aproximadamente?
questions.hint: Esse ponto também é chamado de nascente ou oriente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Num mapa com escala 1:100.000, duas cidades estão a 6 cm de distância. Qual é a distância real em quilômetros?
questions.hint: Cada centímetro vale 1 km.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Num mapa com escala 1:500.000, uma estrada mede 4 cm. Qual é o comprimento real da estrada em quilômetros?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Num mapa com escala 1:2.000.000, a distância entre duas capitais é de 15 cm. Qual é a distância real em quilômetros?
questions.hint: Primeiro descubra quantos quilômetros vale 1 cm.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que tipo de escala é representada por uma barra dividida em partes, com as distâncias escritas?
questions.hint: Ela é um desenho, não uma fração.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual mapa mostra mais detalhes de uma área?
options: Um mapa de grande escala, como 1:10.000
Um mapa de pequena escala, como 1:10.000.000
Os dois mostram a mesma quantidade de detalhes
questions.answer: Um mapa de grande escala, como 1:10.000
questions.hint: Quanto menor o número do denominador, menor a redução.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma cidade está à esquerda de outra num mapa com o norte para cima. Em que direção ela está?
questions.hint: Com o norte para cima, o leste fica à direita.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: No mapa de uma cidade, com escala 1:50.000, o caminho da escola até o parque mede 3 cm. Qual é a distância real em metros?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que é importante que um mapa tenha legenda e escala? Explique em 1 ou 2 frases.
questions.hint: Pense no que você não conseguiria saber sem esses dois elementos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Imagine que você vai desenhar o mapa do caminho da sua casa até a escola. Que elementos você incluiria e por quê?
questions.hint: Lembre-se de título, legenda, escala e orientação.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Scratch, what is a variable?
options: A named storage place that holds a value
questions.answer: A named storage place that holds a value
questions.hint: Think of a labelled box.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which Scratch block category do you use to create a new variable?
questions.hint: It is usually an orange category.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which block would you use to add 1 to a score each time a sprite collects a coin?
questions.hint: One block replaces the value, the other adds to it.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does the block "set score to 0" do?
options: Makes the value of score exactly 0
questions.answer: Makes the value of score exactly 0
questions.hint: 'Set' replaces the old value.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What word describes giving a variable its starting value at the beginning of a program?
questions.hint: It begins with 'init…'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Where is the best place to put "set score to 0" in a game?
options: Under "when green flag clicked", before the game starts
Inside the loop that checks for coins
At the very end of the game
questions.answer: Under "when green flag clicked", before the game starts
questions.hint: The score should reset only once, when a new game begins.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A variable lives starts at 3. The program runs "change lives by -1" twice. What is the value of lives now?
questions.hint: Subtract 1 each time.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: score is set to 10. Then the program runs "change score by 5" and then "set score to 2". What is score now?
questions.hint: Look carefully at the last block.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A timer variable starts at 30. Inside a loop, the program waits 1 second and changes timer by -1. After 12 loops, what is timer?
questions.hint: How much has been taken away in total?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why is a good variable name like "score" better than "x1"?
options: It makes the program easier to read and understand
It makes the program run faster
questions.answer: It makes the program easier to read and understand
questions.hint: Think about someone else reading your code.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What happens if you forget to reset the score at the start of a game?
options: The new game starts with the score from the last game
questions.answer: The new game starts with the score from the last game
questions.hint: Variables keep their value until something changes them.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which condition would end a countdown game when time runs out?
questions.hint: A countdown goes down to a certain number.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the difference between "For all sprites" and "For this sprite only" when creating a variable?
options: All sprites can use it, or only one sprite can use it
One is faster than the other
One stores numbers and the other stores words
questions.answer: All sprites can use it, or only one sprite can use it
questions.hint: Think about who is allowed to see and change the variable.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A program has "repeat 4" containing "change total by 3". total starts at 0. What is the final value of total?
questions.hint: The loop runs 4 times.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe how you would use two variables, score and timer, in a simple catching game.
questions.hint: Explain what each variable starts at and when it changes.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why a variable is useful in a game instead of writing a fixed number.
questions.hint: Think about values that change while the game is running.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a first draft?
options: The first complete version of a piece of writing, which can be improved
A plan written in bullet points only
questions.answer: The first complete version of a piece of writing, which can be improved
questions.hint: Writers expect to change it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which activity focuses mainly on improving content, structure and vocabulary?
questions.hint: One looks at the big picture; the other checks small errors.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which activity focuses on checking spelling, punctuation and grammar errors?
questions.hint: It is usually the last step before you hand work in.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Put these stages in the best order.
questions.hint: You cannot check errors in writing that does not exist yet.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the spelling: "The castle was definately haunted." Write the correct word.
questions.hint: Look for the word 'finite' inside it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the spelling: "I recieved a letter yesterday." Write the correct word.
questions.hint: Remember: i before e except after c.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.hint: The exclamation mark belongs inside the speech marks.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best way to fix this run-on sentence? "The storm arrived we ran inside."
options: The storm arrived, so we ran inside.
The storm arrived we, ran inside.
The storm, arrived we ran inside.
The storm arrived we ran, inside.
questions.answer: The storm arrived, so we ran inside.
questions.hint: Two main clauses need a connective or a full stop.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which revision replaces a weak verb with a more precise one? "The fox went across the field."
options: The fox darted across the field.
The fox went quickly across the field.
The fox did go across the field.
The fox went across a field.
questions.answer: The fox darted across the field.
questions.hint: Look for a single, vivid verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word should replace "nice" to make this sentence more vivid? "We had a nice view of the mountains."
questions.hint: Choose the word that shows the strongest feeling.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.hint: "It's" always means "it is" or "it has".

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best strategy for proofreading your own writing?
options: Read it slowly, aloud if possible, checking one line at a time
questions.answer: Read it slowly, aloud if possible, checking one line at a time
questions.hint: Your eyes skip errors when you read fast.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A paragraph jumps between three different ideas. What is the best way to redraft it?
options: Split it into separate paragraphs, each with one main idea
questions.answer: Split it into separate paragraphs, each with one main idea
questions.hint: Each paragraph should have a clear focus.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: "Their / There / They're going to the museum tomorrow."
questions.hint: Which one means "they are"?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain the difference between editing and proofreading, using an example of each.
questions.hint: Think about big changes versus small corrections.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Improve this sentence and explain one change you made: "It was a big house and it was old and it was scary."
questions.hint: Think about combining ideas and choosing stronger adjectives.
